title: fix(mcp): describe_object says whose words a field description carries
body:

_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBLW6dHPW6sSheA32XPKZzPV)_
repo:objectstack#3 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzg2evNa1V3zxrQq3KX

Closes #34877
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:MCP `describe_object` 工具说明里关于字段 `description` 的那半句,从「description (where written)」改为「description (where set: the author's, or the platform's on a column it injects)」。返回内容本身不变。
- 为什么改:旧句让客户端以为每条字段描述都是应用作者写的。实测 CRM 示例 6 个对象共返回 48 条字段描述,全部来自平台注入列(`organization_id`、`created_at`、`owner_id`、`queue` 等,均带 `system: true`),作者写的字段描述为 0 条。
- 风险与回滚:只改一行工具说明文字,不动返回形状、元数据或契约;两条传输(HTTP 与 stdio)共用同一处注册。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:① `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` 的 `describe_object` description(新句);② `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.object-descriptions-34721.test.ts` 末尾新增的 `[#34877]` 块;③ `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-object-descriptions-34721.test.ts` 新增的 `[#34877]` 用例(真实引擎注入的列)。
- 两分钟验证:在仓根执行 `pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp exec vitest run src/stdio-data-bridge.object-descriptions-34721.test.ts`,预期 5 个测试全部通过。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

`describe_object`'s tool description (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`, the one registration both transports share) said each field carries a `description (where written)`, beside an object description `(where the author wrote one)`. A client reads that as "every field description is the app author's text". The field clause now reads:

> description (where set: the author's, or the platform's on a column it injects)

The object clauses of `list_objects` and `describe_object` are unchanged: the measurement below shows an object's description is always its author's.

No answer key, value or input schema moves. Changeset: `@objectstack/mcp` patch.

## Premise, measured on `origin/main` `db1a05cdaee`

`describe_object` on the `examples/app-crm` objects, through the real HTTP bridge (`ObjectQL` + `SqlDriver` + `SecurityPlugin` + `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation`, the harness of `mcp-object-descriptions-34721.test.ts`, with the six CRM objects registered as an app). This was a one-off scratch run, not committed.

| object | fields | with description | platform-injected (`system: true`) | author-declared |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `crm_account` | 12 | 8 | 8 | 0 |
| `crm_contact` | 13 | 8 | 8 | 0 |
| `crm_opportunity` | 20 | 8 | 8 | 0 |
| `crm_opportunity_line_item` | 13 | 8 | 8 | 0 |
| `crm_lead` | 21 | 8 | 8 | 0 |
| `crm_activity` | 18 | 8 | 8 | 0 |

That is 48 of 48 field descriptions from the platform and 0 from the author. On every object they belong to the same eight columns: `organization_id`, `created_at`, `created_by`, `updated_at`, `updated_by`, `owner_id`, `owning_business_unit_id`, `queue`. Example: `created_at` answers `"Timestamp when the record was created (auto-populated by the driver)."` with `system: true` (the text of `AUDIT_FIELD_DEFS` in `packages/spec/src/data/injected-system-column-provenance.ts`). No CRM field declares a `description`; the source agrees (`grep description examples/app-crm/src/objects/*.object.ts` hits only object descriptions, validation-rule descriptions and a field named `description`).

All six object descriptions are the author's text (for example, `crm_account`: "A company that the org sells to or supports."), in both `describe_object` and `list_objects`. The registry injects no object-level description. Its only object-description writer is an `objectExtensions` merge, which carries another package author's text.

The card says "most". The measurement says all, on this app. The content of the descriptions is correct (it is the platform's own column text), so only the sentence was wrong. The premise is no wider than filed.

Contract check: the sentence is pinned by no snapshot, test, ADR or spec descriptor. `packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts` lists only tool names. `grep` for both phrases across the repo (minus `node_modules`) hits only `mcp-http-tools.ts`. So `Clause-②: no` stands. Twins: none. The stdio transport registers the same `registerObjectTools`, and no skill text, doc or README restates the clause.

## Tests

- `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.object-descriptions-34721.test.ts`, new top-level `[#34877]` block. Through the real tools over the stdio bridge, it asserts that the `describe_object` description carries the new clause and no longer carries `description (where written)`, and that an injected column (`created_at`, served as the registry serves it) is answered with the platform's description and `system: true`, beside an authored field with `system: false`. The existing `list_objects` `fieldCount` moves 4 to 5 because the fixture gained that column.
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-object-descriptions-34721.test.ts`, new `[#34877]` case. On the real engine (nothing faked about injection), `created_at` and `owner_id` come back with `AUDIT_FIELD_DEFS` / `OWNER_FIELD_DEF` descriptions and `system: true`, and the authored `amount` with `system: false`.

Red/green: the old sentence was put back on disk through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor 1 to 0, blob `9a18605c784c` to `5991f3f107e4`). The stdio file went red: `1 failed | 4 passed`, `expected 'Get the schema of a data object as yo…' to contain 'description (where set: the author\'s…'`. After the restore the blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty. The injected-column assertions pin existing behaviour (no source behaviour changed), so they get no ablation.

## Acceptance notes

- The unreleased `.changeset/34721-mcp-object-descriptions.md` (from the PR that added the key) says the tools return "the description an author wrote on … its fields". That is the same claim this card corrects. It is left untouched here, because editing an existing changeset is out of this card's scope. This PR's own changeset states the correction, so both ship in the same release notes.
- In the code, the helper is named `authoredDescription` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`, `packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts`), with JSDoc saying "authored". That is internal naming, not client-facing, and is not changed.
- An author who declares an audit column (for example `created_at`) keeps their own description, while governance forces `system: true` on it. The new clause covers this, because it says "a column it injects" and does not say "every `system` field".
